title: Undeciphered: the Byblos syllabary
summary: Fourteen inscriptions from Byblos use a script still classed as undeciphered. The corpus is considered too small for internal analysis, and claimed decipherments have not won acceptance.
why: A whole Bronze Age writing system from a major Levantine port remains silent.

notes.problem: The 2024 assessment judged one proposal (Woudhuizen/Best), not all proposed decipherments.
Open question had no theories (schema requires 2-4).

question: Can the Byblos syllabary be read, and what language does it record?
evidence: Fourteen known inscriptions; sign counts estimated from about 90 to 114; a 2024 assessment found the Woudhuizen–Best decipherment scientifically inadequate.
wouldSettle: New inscriptions, ideally a bilingual, enlarging the corpus enough for systematic decipherment.

theories.name: Early West Semitic
theories.idea: Mendenhall (1985) read an 'Old Coastal' Semitic language; Colless supports it, but translations are often cryptic.

theories.name: Northwest Semitic near Akkadian
theories.idea: Best reads temple-building records; a 2024 critique found the Woudhuizen/Best translations scientifically inadequate.

theories.name: Phoenician
theories.idea: Dhorme (1946) read a Phoenician word for 'in the year' and proposed values for 75 signs.
